java_locations.role: Defines the ordinary message endpoint grammar symmetrically for PART1 and PART2. Each side accepts a code `[%pLN_.@]+`, a quoted long name, a quoted long name followed by `as` and a code, or a code followed by `as` and a quoted long name. getOrCreateParticipant projects every alternative to one participant code plus one display value before creating or reusing the participant.
Registers CommandArrow in the first relevant UML factory, so every line matching the complete endpoint-and-arrow grammar participates in Sequence factory viability.

Requires one registered command to consume each complete line. A Java-valid CommandArrow endpoint form therefore keeps Sequence viable; it is not optional token syntax considered after factory selection.

rust_locations.role: Uses one regex capture per endpoint, restricted to a quoted string or `\w+`. It cannot consume either inline `as` ordering and excludes dots and at signs from bare codes. try_message then merely unquotes each capture and uses the same string as both participant id and implicit label, so the Rust message model cannot represent Java's distinct code/display projection for inline aliases.

Runs the same SeqParser over the whole command stream. Because try_message cannot consume Java's alias endpoint forms, the entire Sequence factory candidate is rejected before subtype ownership is chosen.
Already stores participant identity and display label separately and messages refer to participant ids, so the AST can carry the Java code/display result once endpoint parsing produces it.

Uses sequence::factory_accepts and sequence::looks_like_message as ownership inputs, then dispatches only the selected parser. Incomplete endpoint grammar therefore changes both factory selection and the materialized diagram, producing DESCRIPTION for the preserved Java SEQUENCE source.

claimed_invariant: An ordinary Sequence CommandArrow endpoint is a parsed value with separate participant code and display text. The four Java alternatives are semantically equivalent endpoint constructors on both sides of the arrow: bare code maps code and display to that code; quoted long name maps code and display to the unquoted name; `"Long Name" as code` maps code to `code` and display to `Long Name`; and `code as "Long Name"` maps the same pair in the opposite lexical order. Codes admit Unicode letters/numbers plus underscore, dot, and at sign. This complete endpoint grammar must be shared by Sequence factory viability and actual message parsing, so every Java-valid form selects Sequence and creates/reuses participants by code rather than by display text.
causal_divergence: The preserved `quoted_alias_endpoints` source is accepted by Java CommandArrow on all three lines: each inline alias yields participant codes `Node.code`, `Component.code`, and `Queue.code`, while the quoted strings become their displayed names. Rust MESSAGE_RE has no `as` alternatives and its bare branch is only `\w+`; SeqParser::try_message therefore returns false on the first line, factory_accepts rejects Sequence, and later UML scoring selects a DESCRIPTION-backed model. This is not a reserved-word score imbalance. It is an incomplete ordinary endpoint parser coupled to a model path that conflates lexical endpoint text with both id and label.
planned_model_change: Introduce one anchored ordinary-message endpoint parser that returns a typed `{ code, display }` value for all four Java CommandArrow alternatives, including dotted and at-sign codes. Compose the full message grammar from two such endpoints and the existing arrow/style/activation/message-tail grammar. Use that same parsed result for looks_like_message, factory_accepts, and SeqParser::try_message; ensure participants by `code`, retain `display` when implicitly creating them, and preserve an existing participant's declaration-owned display on reuse according to the current participant model. Keep external-message endpoint grammar separate because Java handles it through CommandExoArrow rather than CommandArrow.
perturbation_axes: endpoint ordering: quoted-long-name AS code versus code AS quoted-long-name, independently on source and target
code alphabet: simple, dotted, at-sign, mixed Unicode letter/number, and underscore codes
identity/display reuse: aliases introduced by a message, aliases reused by later messages, and aliases predeclared with a different declaration order
arrow grammar: forward, reverse, dotted, bidirectional, styled, activation-suffixed, and labelled messages
endpoint position and cardinality: alias on only one side, both sides, self-message, cycles, and multicast controls
factory controls: syntactically similar class/description relationships and malformed alias forms that Java CommandArrow rejects
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns ordinary CommandArrow endpoint parsing, typed code/display projection, implicit participant identity, and use of that parser by Sequence factory viability. It does not own explicit participant-declaration grammar, external-message commands, general Class-versus-Description fallback after Sequence genuinely rejects a line, participant layout, note geometry, SVG serialization, comparator slack, baselines, park lists, syntax-error markers, or guard allow-lists.
acceptance: The preserved Java-success counterexample `quoted_alias_endpoints.puml` produces a zero byte-level no-oracle diff; Java and Rust both emit SEQUENCE and the participant ids/displays follow CommandArrow's code/display projection.
Fresh valid inputs cover both inline alias orderings, aliases on both endpoint positions, and dotted plus at-sign codes; every Java-success input has a zero byte-level no-oracle diff.

Fresh reuse inputs prove that code, not display text, is participant identity across reordered and repeated messages without duplicating participants or overwriting declaration-owned presentation incorrectly.
Fresh malformed and non-CommandArrow controls remain rejected by Sequence exactly when Java rejects them, allowing the same later UML factory owner or syntax result.
Parser-focused tests prove one shared endpoint parser drives actual messages, looks_like_message, and factory_accepts rather than three drifting recognizers.

An independent checker at the exact implementation revision generates at least two fresh independent axes, requires Java exit zero, preserves all artifacts, and records REJECT for any nonzero no-oracle diff.
forbidden_approaches: special-casing the labels, codes, reserved words, or three lines in quoted_alias_endpoints
adding subtype score weights so Sequence wins without accepting and materializing the Java endpoint grammar
stripping `as` text ad hoc without preserving separate code and display values
loosening the endpoint regex to an unstructured catch-all that accepts Java-invalid commands
post-processing SVG ids, labels, diagram type, or coordinates
changing comparator controls, baselines, skip rules, park lists, syntax-error markers, or guard allow-lists
